name: Null Signal // Static City Tour Tee
description:
Null Signal is a post-industrial noise collective out of the Shelf's lower grid — three musicians, a rotating cast of sound designers, and a visual artist named Yolanda Ferris who does all their merch by hand-screening in batches of forty or fifty at a time. The Static City Tour Tee is the shirt from their 2199 run through six underground venues across the Chicago-Milwaukee corridor. The design is a dense overlapping cityscape rendered in grainy halftone — the kind that reads as abstraction from a distance and resolves into the silhouette of the Spire as you get closer. Printed in silver ink on a black heavyweight cotton-analog tee.

The printing is slightly uneven — Ferris doesn't sweat registration errors — and the silver has a subtle metallic quality that catches light in dim venues. The shirt is cut boxy and runs a size large. Most people wearing it either saw the shows or know someone who did. A small number are just fans who traded for one online. It's been bootlegged twice, both times noticeably worse.
what_it_says: You were in the room. Or you at least know what rooms matter.
manufacturer: Null Signal (independent — Yolanda Ferris, screen printer)
story_hooks: One of the forty-three shirts from the first night's batch was printed on a shirt that already had something written on the inside collar — in a language the band doesn't recognize.
Null Signal's lead vocalist went missing two weeks after the tour ended. The shirt has become something of a memorial object in certain circles.
A Tier 4 streetwear label wants to license the Static City design for a collaboration. Ferris has not responded to any messages.

physical_description.visual_profile: Boxy, deliberately oversized silhouette with a dense halftone cityscape graphic across the chest that resolves into the Spire's outline on close inspection. Street-level underground music merchandise with hand-screened authenticity. Reads as abstract noise from distance, architectural detail up close.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, intentionally oversized — runs large. Drops to mid-hip, generous through shoulders and sleeves. Comfortable, non-fitted cut suited to layering or solo wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight cotton-analog blend, substantial weight and natural drape with synthetic durability
physical_description.texture: Slightly rough hand-screened surface, grainy halftone texture from manual printing process. Silver ink sits proud on fabric surface with subtle tactile quality. Uneven registration adds organic, artisanal wear
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep black base with silver metallic ink graphic. Silver catches light in venues and dim spaces, creating subtle shimmer. No additional accent colors — monochromatic with metallic highlight
distinctive_features: Hand-screened silver halftone graphic by Yolanda Ferris — uneven registration intentional
Overlapping cityscape resolves into Spire silhouette at closer viewing distance
Metallic silver ink with light-catching properties
Limited batch printing — batches of 40-50 units
Tour documentation: 'Static City Tour' implicit in design, six venue corridor run 2199
Visible screen imperfections and ink inconsistencies as mark of authenticity
Boxy cut signals underground/independent rather than corporate retail
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 crossover — affordable independent merch, social capital in underground scenes exceeds material value. Not luxury, not salvage, but culturally weighted above price point
physical_description.cultural_context: Post-industrial noise collective aesthetic. Wearer signals underground music venue participation, post-corporate creative DIY ethos, rejection of mass retail. Bootleg versions circulate but carry stigma — authenticity verified by Ferris's characteristic printing inconsistencies
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after wear, but holds up well. Silver ink develops subtle patina from venue sweat and moisture. Fading along creases and neckline natural over time. Creases and wrinkles from storage and movement add character rather than detract
